correctness.rationale: Full antipodal moments give the exact quartic force -(I+M|x|²)x-2Sx. A common homothetic acceleration therefore forces each representative vector into an eigenspace of S; tracing each eigenspace gives the unique frame condition and r_a²=C/(M+4W_a/d_a), with C>0. Conversely those equations give the same force coefficient Lambda=I+C at every particle. The scalar quartic oscillator has a conserved energy, finite quarter-period beta integral, and least labeled period four times that quarter. For m=d, a square Parseval frame forces orthogonality, deriving uniqueness and the sharp d-radius bound. Standalone checker.py independently evaluates full exact 2m-body force sums for 201 finite orthogonal examples plus a two-block trine example and numerically compares the oscillator first zero to the analytic beta time. Finite tests do not establish the general theorem; the algebra and ODE energy argument do.

value.rationale: The exact inverse classification asks which natural antipodal shapes support a coherent self-similar many-body orbit under the positive-quartic interaction. The answer replaces a coupled 2m-particle force system with an invariant eigenspace partition, positive weighted unit tight frames, and a compulsory algebraic mass-to-radius rule, allowing several unequal radii. The complete all-dimensional criterion, sharp upper bound of d radial classes, and mass-specific minimal 2d-body uniqueness provide a structural geometric description beyond a trivial substitution or finite re-tabulation. The period is a useful dynamically explicit consequence, not independently novel.
